titulo: From chat to queue: why keep your tasks
lead: In chat, the agent does one thing at a time, and only while the window is open. A durable queue keeps every request, runs them one at a time, picks up again after a crash, and separates what worked from what failed.
objetivo: explain the four guarantees of a durable queue and why they let you walk away.
hero_alt: A row of paper slips in sequence on a dark table, one of them highlighted.

aprende.t: The limit of chat: you have to be watching
The four guarantees of a durable queue
The states of a task, from request to result
Where inemaccbot comes in at step 3

secoes.sub: The same request, in two different places.

nos.detalhe: In chat, you type, wait, copy, and paste. If you close the window or the computer shuts off, the work in progress is gone. Ten tasks = ten waits with you sitting in front of it.
The request is saved before it runs. In inemaccbot, the queue is a SQLite database on disk; in the homemade queue, it's one file per task in a folder. Shut down? The task is still there.

itens.t: Picks up what was left halfway

nos.detalhe: A worker takes a task, hands it to the agent, and waits. If the process crashes midway, the next time it starts up it recovers what was in flight before accepting new work.
Each task ends in a clear state: it worked (with the file or text) or it failed (with the reason). That's what you check in the morning.

secoes.volta: Running again only picks up what's left
secoes.legenda: In inemaccbot the request arrives through Telegram; in the homemade queue from lesson 3, it's a .md file in a folder. The idea is the same.

rolagem_fim.titulo: Why this lets you walk away
rolagem_fim.texto: Save before running, one at a time, resume after a crash, and keep done separate from failed: with these four guarantees, turning off the screen doesn't cost you any work.

secoes.sub: What you should expect from any queue, homemade or not.

texto: The request becomes a record on disk the moment it arrives. It doesn't depend on an open window or on the program's memory.
In inemaccbot, each request becomes a job in a database table. It has a number (j13), a queue, a status, and how many attempts are left.

exemplo.texto: You send the request from your phone, the computer restarts, and the request is still on the list.

texto: Each worker takes one task, finishes it, and only then takes the next. This prevents two jobs from fighting over the same machine.
In inemaccbot there are five queues with different limits: the rendering queue runs one at a time on purpose, because it uses the graphics card; the network queue accepts ten.
If the process crashes midway, the task isn't lost or left half-done forever. The next time it starts up, whatever was in progress goes back to the queue.

inemaccbot does this before accepting new work and writes to the log: boot: recuperação de leases — requeued=N failed=M. Requeued is what went back to the queue; failed is what had already used up all its attempts.
A task that hit an error doesn't vanish and doesn't block the queue: it goes to the failures side, with the reason written down, and the queue moves on.
The inemaccbot prompts require the agent to finish with RESULT: <path> or ERRO: <short reason>. That contract is what lets you know, without opening anything, how each task ended.

secoes.sub: The names change from one queue to another; the idea is the same.

blocos.conteudo:
fila/
  entrada/   # requests waiting their turn
  rodando/   # the task the agent is working on right now
  feito/     # request + answer
  falhou/    # request + ERRO and the reason

queued    # in the queue, waiting its turn
running   # a worker picked it up and is executing it
done      # finished with a result
failed    # ran out of attempts, with the reason
canceled  # you canceled it (/cancelar)

abas.html:
• Homemade queue: when you run it again, whatever is in rodando/ goes back to entrada/.
  • inemaccbot: the worker renews a "lease" on the task while it works. If the lease expires because the process crashed, the task goes back to queued as long as there are attempts left.

abas.rot: Who decides what counts as a failure
abas.html: In the home-made queue: an empty response or an error code from the agent. In inemaccbot: the agent did not finish with RESULT:, the deadline (timeout) ran out, or the attempts (max_tentativas, 2 to 4 in the catalog skills) were used up.

secoes.sub: The durable queue of inemaccbot and the approval gate, in a minute and a half.
The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: What is the key difference between asking in the chat and sending to a durable queue?
opcoes: In the queue, the request is saved to disk before it runs, so it does not depend on you or on an open window.
The queue uses a better AI model.
In the chat, you cannot ask for long tasks.
perguntas.explica: The model can be the same. What changes is the place: the request becomes a durable record, so it survives crashes and can run while you are away.

perguntas.p: The bot log showed requeued=2 failed=1 on startup. What happened?
opcoes: The database was erased and recreated.
Three new tasks arrived during the night.
The previous process crashed with work in progress: two tasks went back to the queue and one had already used up its attempts.
Two tasks succeeded and one failed.
perguntas.explica: This line appears on startup and is the evidence that there was work in flight when the process crashed. Requeued goes back to the queue; failed had no attempts left.

perguntas.p: A task failed at 3 a.m. What does a good queue do?
opcoes: Stops everything until you wake up.
Records the failure with the reason and moves on to the next task.
Deletes the task so it does not get in the way.
perguntas.explica: The failure is kept separate, with a reason, and the queue keeps moving. Retrying forever would burn the whole night (and money); that is why there is a maximum number of attempts.
